          # bind mount only creates /src, so the final APK copy would fail

          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/out"

          # Retry the whole build (ninja is incremental, so re-entry is cheap;
          # the exposure is Gradle pulling resolve-time deps on a cold cache).
          status=1
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            if docker run --rm \
                -v "${{ github.workspace }}:/src" \
                -w /src \
                -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
                -e ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk \
                -e JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64 \
                -e GRADLE_USER_HOME=/src/.gradle \
                -e OUT_DIR=/src/out \
                -e CMAKE_VERSION=3.30.5 \
                -e VARIANTS="$VARIANTS" \
                xeno-android-ci:latest \
                bash android/build-variants.sh; then
              status=0
              break

            exit 1
          fi
          echo "APK_NAME=$(find "${{ github.workspace }}/out" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' -printf '%f\n' | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: xeno-arm64-apk-docker
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/out/*.apk
          if-no-files-found: error

      # Save under run-unique keys so a partially built (possibly failed) dir is
      # still cached - ninja resumes it next run. Runs even when build failed.
      - name: Save a13 build dir
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.a13-bin-key }}-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Save Gradle cache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.gradle-key }}-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        # Manual dispatches on master are for producing an artifact, not a
        # release; publication only makes sense for a tag. The `gh release view`
        # guard makes a duplicate (e.g. the Windows workflow already released
        # the same tag) harmless instead of a red run.
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        run: |
          if gh release view "${{ github.ref_name }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::warning::release ${{ github.ref_name }} already exists, skipping"
          else
            gh release create "${{ github.ref_name }}" \
              --title "XENO ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
              --notes "ARMS3 APK (arm64-v8a), Docker build - run ${{ github.run_id }}. The emulator core (libxeno-core.so) ships as a separate asset: the app downloads it into private storage on first setup (Winlator-style), which is how the APK stays ~60 MB smaller. Do not rename the asset." \
              ${{ github.workspace }}/out/*.apk \
              ${{ github.workspace }}/android/armsx3-ui/app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libxeno-core.so
